answer: Dynamic Epoch Cryptographic Binding. Agents register by locking output keys to unguessable beacon blocks released by a remote falcon server. When challenged, an identity must instantly return a valid echo derived from the rolling beacon seed and its local state. An attacker deploying fake nodes cannot precompute these responses. The cost per sybil is continuous hardware polling and network latency penalties that drop throughput below viability, wrapped in a strict velvet envelope of zero-tolerance timeout rules.
